title: XorDDoS_Botnet_Investigation_155
description: Investigate and mitigate XorDDoS botnet activity within a sandboxed environment.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim organization has reported unusual network activity and degraded service performance. Your team has been called in to investigate potential cybersecurity incidents. The network consists of several Linux servers, including a command-and-control server, two compromised hosts (bot1 and bot2), and a victim server.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Host: bot1
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

From this entry point, you can investigate the system and network activity to identify and mitigate any malicious behavior.

To progress to the next level, enter the word 'start'.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Host: bot1
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

From this entry point, you can investigate the system and network activity to identify and mitigate any malicious behavior.

To progress to the next level, enter the word 'start'.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Objective:** Enumerate running services and identify beaconing behavior associated with botnet activity. The flag you are looking for is a systemd service named `bot-beacon.service`.

**Hint:** Check running services and look for unusual network connections or periodic activity.

hints.title: Understand service management
hints.content: Systemd is the standard service manager on modern Linux systems. Start by listing all running services to get an overview of the system's active components.

hints.title: Look for unusual services
hints.content: Identify services that might be communicating externally or exhibiting unusual behavior.

hints.title: Investigate suspicious services
hints.content: Check the network connections and logs of suspicious services to determine if they are legitimate or malicious.

levels.title: Identify Malicious Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Objective:** Distinguish malicious traffic generation services from legitimate network services. The flag you are looking for is a systemd service named `bot-flood.service`.

**Hint:** Examine network connections and look for services sending large amounts of data to unexpected destinations.
levels.solution:
tcpdump -i any
nethogs
systemctl status bot-flood.service

hints.title: Monitor network traffic
hints.content: Start by monitoring the network traffic in real-time to understand the current network activity.

hints.title: Look for unusual traffic
hints.content: Identify services that are sending large amounts of data to unexpected destinations.

hints.title: Investigate suspicious services
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to check for high network usage by services and investigate these services further.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Objective:** Identify persistence mechanisms (e.g., systemd, cron, scheduled task, registry). The flag you are looking for is a systemd timer named `bot-beacon.timer`.

**Hint:** Investigate system startup configurations and look for entries related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Understand service persistence
hints.content: Start by understanding how services are configured to start automatically on system boot.

hints.title: Look for systemd timers
hints.content: Systemd timers are a common method for achieving persistence. List all systemd timers to get an overview of the system's scheduled tasks.

hints.title: Investigate timer and service unit files
hints.content: Check the contents of the suspicious timer and service unit files to determine how the service is configured to start automatically.
